claim: On PCIe GPU systems without a dedicated scale-up fabric, intra-node GPU traffic and NIC-based inter-node traffic share the same PCIe hierarchy, so concurrent transfers contend on bottleneck links and aggregate AlltoAllv throughput collapses well below nominal link rates.
stance_target: the repo's claim that a PCIe-only fabric cannot support the all-to-all traffic that expert parallelism requires
scope_conditions: PCIe GPU clusters with shared PCIe switches and links; non-Clos topologies; Gen4/Gen5 x16 testbeds
quoted_support: Without a dedicated scale-up interconnect (e.g., NVLink or Infinity Fabric), PCIe GPU systems carry both intra-node and inter-node traffic through the PCIe hierarchy, where concurrent transfers can contend for PCIe link bandwidth.

claim: Topology-aware AlltoAllv scheduling yields average speedups of 5.88x over FAST and 1.72x over DeepEP across four PCIe platforms up to 256 GPUs, showing that PCIe all-to-all is far from the hardware limit when paths are chosen to avoid contention.
stance_target: the strong form of 'expert parallelism is ruled out by the fabric' — the fabric is bad, but the software stack on top of it is also leaving large factors on the table
scope_conditions: 32 R5080-CX8 nodes, 8 R5080-BF3 nodes, 4 R5090-BF3 nodes, 2 L20-CX7 nodes; two-tier leaf-spine; random-demand, skew and uniform AlltoAllv
quoted_support: Evaluation on four platforms (up to 256 GPUs) shows average AlltoAllv speedups of 5.88x over FAST and 1.72x over DeepEP.

claim: On 256 GPUs, AlltoAllv algorithmic bandwidth reaches 30.91 GB/s with topology-aware scheduling versus 28.11 GB/s for DeepEP and 18.85 GB/s for NCCL, i.e. the best PCIe all-to-all is roughly 1.6x NCCL's.
stance_target: what per-rank all-to-all bandwidth is realistically achievable on a PCIe fabric, as a ceiling for what a Gen2 x4 box could hope for
scope_conditions: 256x RTX 5080 across 32 nodes, hidden dim 7168, top-k 8, M=128 input tokens per rank
quoted_support: VarioPath achieves the highest algorithmic bandwidth at all eight values of M and reaches 30.91 GB/s at M = 128, compared with 28.11 GB/s for DeepEP and 18.85 GB/s for NCCL.

claim: Replacing NCCL's AlltoAllv with topology-aware scheduling reduces Qwen3-30B-A3B prefill latency by 19.1% to 27.2% across EP16, EP24 and EP32, with the reduction growing as expert-parallel degree increases.
stance_target: the claim that EP communication cost scales with EP degree and sits on the prefill critical path
scope_conditions: two to four R5080-BF3 nodes, EP16/EP24/EP32, 8,192-token prefill, 15 requests per point
quoted_support: For Qwen3-30B-A3B, replacing the exchange with VarioPath reduces prefill latency by 19.1-27.2% across EP16, EP24, and EP32. The reduction increases with the expert-parallel degree because expert dispatch and combine lie on the prefill critical path.

claim: Peer-path co-design is necessary on PCIe: fixing either the peer matching or the physical path roughly doubles AlltoAllv completion time (2.03x and 2.00x), and fixing both raises it to 2.84x.
stance_target: whether a simple ring or nearest-path schedule is adequate for EP on a PCIe box
scope_conditions: two-node R5080-BF3, five skew AlltoAllv demand matrices with Zipf s=0.6
quoted_support: Table 3 shows that fixing either dimension approximately doubles completion time, while fixing both increases it to 2.84x that of the unrestricted design. Thus, peer-path co-design is necessary to retain the unrestricted design's performance on this workload.
numbers: 2.84x fixed nearest path + fixed peer rotation

claim: AlltoAllv demand in MoE changes at every layer, with per-layer execution times often below one millisecond, so a static communication schedule cannot track the routing pattern.
stance_target: the claim that EP's data-dependent communication is a poor fit for a fabric that needs careful static scheduling
scope_conditions: MoE inference with per-layer routing recomputation
quoted_support: In MoE inference, token-to-expert assignments are recomputed at every layer, producing a new AlltoAllv demand matrix. With per-layer execution times often below one millisecond, the scheduler may need to adapt to each new demand matrix on a similarly short timescale.

claim: PCIe systems are widely deployed at production scale for inference (Alibaba and ByteDance run thousands of PCIe-connected T4 and L40S GPUs; Cloudflare runs multiple PCIe GPU types for Workers AI), so PCIe-only training constraints are a mainstream problem rather than an exotic one.
stance_target: the relevance and generality of PCIe-fabric findings
quoted_support: For example, Alibaba and ByteDance deploy PCIe-connected NVIDIA T4 and L40S GPUs in production clusters comprising thousands of GPUs. Cloudflare also deploys multiple types of PCIe GPUs for its Workers AI service.

claim: VarioPath's online scheduler attains 99.18% of the MILP-optimal AlltoAllv bandwidth on average (0.82% optimality gap) while planning in 3.2 to 78 microseconds per emitted activation, so near-optimal PCIe all-to-all scheduling is computationally practical.
stance_target: whether topology-aware EP scheduling is implementable in a training loop rather than only offline
scope_conditions: one- and two-node R5080-BF3; 50 skew AlltoAllv calls; catalog construction 0.8 s (8 GPUs) to 5,673 s (256 GPUs)
quoted_support: Across all 50 instances, VarioPath attains 99.18% of the MILP-optimal bandwidth on average, corresponding to an average optimality gap of 0.82%.

claim: NCCL fixes transport paths at communicator setup and MSCCL inherits those paths, so neither can adapt an active pair's physical path to the current traffic stage — a structural limitation on PCIe topologies.
stance_target: the claim that NCCL's defaults are mismatched to PCIe contention, which matters when estimating what a stock NCCL all-reduce actually achieves on this box
scope_conditions: NCCL and MSCCL on PCIe GPU systems
quoted_support: NCCL fixes transport paths at communicator setup, and MSCCL inherits those paths. Neither baseline can adapt an active pair's physical path to the current stage.
